problem: Zero-shot VLN systems wrap frozen VLMs in human-authored navigation workflows (maps, memory, waypoints, backtracking), and trained policies or dual-brain systems need large navigation data and fixed handoffs. It is unclear how much capability the general-purpose model already holds when it is given control of the loop.
motivation: Frontier VLMs with multi-turn perception, spatial reasoning and tool use already sustain long tool-mediated loops in coding agents. The paper asks whether the model can directly steer every embodied action, so that reasoning and control stay aligned without navigation-specific scaffolding, and where capability sits across model, harness and interface.
key_idea: Give off-the-shelf coding-agent harnesses only monocular RGB (observe) and four discrete primitives (step), so a general-purpose model directly controls the whole embodied loop (agentic embodied control) with no navigation-specific policy, map, memory or planner.
insight: Model choice dominates: swapping the VLM changes SR from 5 to 72, while harness differences are 1.7-7.3 SR and effort changes are inconsistent (-5 to +6, except fable-5 +9.7). A forced waypoint interface helps weak models (+37-38 SR) but is neutral on the strongest models on R2R-CE and hurts on VLNVerse (SR -4 to -6, SPL -20 to -29). Exposing waypoints optionally (hybrid) beats both forced interfaces (76.7 vs 68.3/69), with a coarse-to-fine strategy the agent chooses itself. Failures are silent (23/30 claim success) and route-level, with self-diagnosis without self-correction.
method: Minimal interface: observe() returns one 512x512 front RGB frame without advancing the sim; step(actions) executes up to 50 primitives from FORWARD 0.25m / LEFT 15° / RIGHT 15° / STOP. It returns only the executed count and remaining budget, with no collision, pose or depth.

Generic harnesses: mini-swe-agent, Claude Agent SDK and Codex CLI expose only the bridge tools. The model decides when to observe, act, recover and stop. Fresh session per episode, full history re-sent, no external memory or map. 500-step budget, 200-call cap.
Model/harness/effort sweep: 11+ VLMs (Qwen3.5 4B to opus-5, fable-5, GPT-5.x) crossed with 3 harnesses and vendor reasoning effort, with 3 replications for default-effort Claude SDK cells.
Waypoint arm: replaces primitives with observe() (12-view RGB-D panorama -> trained depth-based waypoint predictor -> 4-view strip with up to 5 numbered candidates), goto(k) and stop(), max 30 gotos.
Hybrid interface: primitives and waypoints exposed together as optional tools; the agent picks when to use each.
Diagnostics: RxR-CE long-horizon stress, 30-failure audit against archived frames (4 categories), VLNVerse/HM-EQA transfer, and 31 exploratory Unitree Go2 real-robot episodes.

setting.backbone: Frozen frontier VLMs (fable-5, opus-5, opus-4.8, sonnet-5, GPT-5.5/5.6, Qwen3.5/3.6/3.7) inside off-the-shelf coding-agent harnesses; hybrid/waypoint arms add a trained waypoint predictor
setting.training_data: none (training-free); the waypoint predictor in the waypoint/hybrid arms is a pretrained SmartWay/ETPNav-style module
setting.observation: monocular front RGB 512x512, HFOV 90° (no depth, pose or panorama in the minimal setting)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP, in bursts of up to 50; optionally waypoint goto(k)
setting.privileged: none (shortest-path and oracle sensors are discarded before reaching the agent)

results: With only monocular RGB and four primitives, zero-shot frontier models reach 68.3-78 SR on R2R-CE rand100, above the AgenticNav zero-shot baseline (55 SR) and in the range of trained Qwen-RobotNav (72) and ABot-N1 (71), although those are reported on the full val-unseen. The hybrid interface reaches 76.7±0.6 SR with about half the steps and under a quarter of the wall time of max-effort primitives. Performance drops to 26-39 SR on RxR-CE, and there are latency and context-growth barriers.
limitations: Long-horizon collapse (RxR-CE SR 26-39), with unbounded context growth and slow wall time (median 206 s per episode, 18.6% over 10 min)
Small n=100 subset with noisy runs (s.d. 1.2-3.5 SR), unmatched serving paths, and comparisons against trained models on a different split; comparison with baselines is not controlled

Silent failures and no motion feedback (step() reports requested rather than realized motion), and weak body and persistent spatial awareness on the real robot (31 qualitative episodes, no success rate)
